name: cloud-search
description: Diego's Cloud Search (#779) - one app for searching what a life in Germany needs, from the owner's design mockup, on the fleet's bottom-nav island: Web Search (House, Jobs, Groceries, Things), Cloud Search (Apps, Messages, Code), Chat (web engines + AI chat), Agents (#913: draft-only agents that read your mail and pages and write drafts you send yourself) and Reports (what agents published). House and Jobs have Listing, Analysis, Feed and Calculators subpages; Search opens Google, DuckDuckGo, Brave or Qwant results in cloud-browser and holds an AI chat over OpenRouter (sessions grouped today / previous 7 days, a model picker over the live catalogue, natively web-searching models flagged, the token read from the fleet Account and never stored here). REAL DATA ONLY: every in-app listing comes from a public API this app is allowed to read (build.json::search.sources), cached on the phone so the last results stay readable offline; a portal whose terms forbid automated access is never fetched - its own search page opens in cloud-browser - and a source that cannot be used at all says why. The German payslip runs the BMF's own Lohnsteuer PAP 2026 (core/pap, generated into Kotlin by core/tools/pap2kt.py) with the 2026 social-insurance rules, golden-tested against the BMF's calculator. English is the base language (#299); dark is the default theme (#336).

android._doc_application_id: The fleet name with its separator dropped, as cloudcalc / clouddrive.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.
auto_update._doc_enabled: Off because this app compiles no libs:updater (#763, see modules._doc): the Store updates it. Kept as data so the release block has the fleet's shape.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph; settings.gradle iterates it. No `logic` lib is compiled in (lib-classes L4): Cloud Search is installed and updated by the Store (SuperApp ▸ Constellation), like Cloud Calc. #797: the app draws its OWN chrome from the owner's mockup (glass theme, top bar), so the fleet kit (libs:ui-kit) is not linked; #868: its bottom nav and sub-page strips are the fleet's (libs:bottomnav).

search-core._doc: Everything the app computes or parses, as a plain-JVM Kotlin module (core/): the build.json::search reader, the source parsers (each against a saved real response in core/src/test/resources/fixtures), filters and sort, the cache-backed query engine, the jobs analysis, the RSS feed, the OpenRouter chat protocol and sessions, and the calculators - the payslip runs the BMF's PAP 2026 generated into tax/Lohnsteuer2026.kt. PIT mutation-tests it on every `gradle test` (core/build.gradle).
search-core._doc_dir: Gradle path :search-core, not :core, so it can never be confused with :libs:core.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which makes this app a fleet mesh member with the debug API (/api/search/* below).

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:text-tools._doc: The ITextTools binder (a `contract` lib): the AI chat reads the OpenRouter token the fleet Account manages through TextToolsClient.revealAiKey(search.ai.account_provider) on use. This app keeps no copy of it - not in prefs, not in a file, not in the debug API.

libs:search-page._doc: #823 the Search page (the engine boxes and the AI chat) as a shared Compose lib, so Cloud Browser draws the same page. This app hosts it (data/SearchHost.kt: ChatFlow, the stores, Browser) and hands it its own glass theme and words (ui/AssistantPages.kt); the lib holds no colour, store, token or network of its own.

libs:bottomnav._doc: #868 the fleet's bottom island (BottomNavIsland) and page-tab strip (PageTabs), and NavDecl, which reads ui.bottom_nav/ui.sections as baked into BuildConfig.

open_with._doc: Where a result URL opens: the constellation fleet row whose package app/build.gradle reads at build time (an unknown id fails the build) for the browser intent and the manifest's <queries>. When that app is not installed, the system's default browser opens it.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds.

unit._doc: `gradle test`: core's JVM suite (BMF golden payslips, calculators, every parser against its saved response, filters, the engine against a fake network and a real cache dir, chat protocol and sessions, this build.json through the parser) followed by its PIT mutation gate, and app's Robolectric smoke test (every vertical reached through the app's own bottom nav and every subpage composed, the menu's categories and Saved Items, Extensive Filters applied, the House market tiles, one Search box per engine, a calculator computed, the debug routes answered).

search._doc: THE declaration (core/Config.kt parses and validates it; app/build.gradle bakes it into BuildConfig.SEARCH_CONFIG_B64; the JVM suite reads this file). No vertical, source, URL, engine, calculator field or model is spelled in Kotlin.
search._doc_cache: A source answer younger than cache_ttl_minutes is reused without asking the source again; an older one is refetched, and when the refetch fails the last stored answer is shown marked stale (the offline last-results view).

search._doc_sources: Every source, with what this app may do with it. kind `api`: a public API read in-app when `enabled` (parser = the core/Listing.kt Parsers branch, held to a saved real response in core/src/test/resources/fixtures). kind `link`: NEVER fetched - the site's own search (or a site: search when its URL scheme needs ids this app cannot know) opens in cloud-browser, because its terms forbid automated access or it has no public API. `why` is shown on the listing under the source's name, so nothing is silently missing. Verified 2026-10-02 from the mesh: BA Jobsuche v6 (200 with the published key and an honest user agent; v4 answers 403), Arbeitnow (200), Open Prices (2,131 Berlin prices within 30 km), search.openfoodfacts.org (200). The fleet's scraping backend was considered for the portals and is not used: crawlee-cloud is archived, and its successor scrappers-api sits behind two-factor auth and returns only a summary from /scrape (the data stays on the server) - and none of the portals below permits scraping in the first place.

ba-jobsuche.label: Bundesagentur für Arbeit
ba-jobsuche.terms: The Federal Employment Agency's public job search API (documented at jobsuche.api.bund.dev); the key is the published client id, not a secret. Verified = an official public source.

arbeitnow.label: Arbeitnow
arbeitnow.terms: 'This is a free public API for jobs, please do not abuse. I would appreciate linking back to the site.' - every card links to the posting. The API cannot search, so the query and the city are applied on the phone (remote jobs are kept in every city).

stepstone.label: StepStone
stepstone.why: No public API, and its terms forbid automated access: its own search opens in cloud-browser.

indeed.label: Indeed
indeed.why: Its publisher API is closed to new partners and its terms forbid scraping: its own search opens in cloud-browser.

series._doc: #797 official time series for a vertical whose analysis is `market`. Each URL returns ONE series (every dimension but time pinned), parsed by `parser` (core/Market.kt Series.parse: jsonstat = Eurostat's JSON-stat 2.0, sdmx_json = SDMX-JSON 1.0 as the Bundesbank and the ECB serve it), cached like a source. change: pct = percent change of an index against the same period a year before; pp = percentage-point change of a rate. Verified 2026-10-03 from the mesh; the ECB's own data API answered an HTML error page on one of two tries, so the mortgage rate is read from the Bundesbank, which publishes the same MFI interest-rate statistic for Germany.

bbk-mortgage-rate.detail: Effective rate on new housing loans to households, Germany
bbk-mortgage-rate.terms: Bundesbank time-series database; free reuse with the source named.

eurostat-house-prices.detail: House price index, all dwellings, Germany (2015 = 100)
eurostat-house-prices.terms: Eurostat dissemination API; reuse authorised with the source named (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU).

eurostat-rents.detail: HICP actual rentals for housing, Germany (2025 = 100)
eurostat-rents.terms: Eurostat dissemination API; reuse authorised with the source named (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU).

feeds._doc: RSS feeds for the Feed subpage; a vertical shows the items whose title or text names one of its feed_keywords.

rent_vs_buy.label: Rent vs Buy
rent_vs_buy.blurb: Month by month: whoever pays less invests the difference; the renter also invests the buyer's upfront cash.
notes: Purchase costs default to Berlin: Grunderwerbsteuer 6.0% + notary and land registry about 2.0% + the buyer's broker share 3.57%.

max_rent.label: Max rent ratio
max_rent.blurb: The rule of thumb: warm rent at most a third of net income.

payslip.label: German Payslip (2026)
payslip.blurb: Company cost → gross → net, monthly. Wage tax by the BMF's own PAP 2026.

warnings.minijob: At or below the 2026 minijob limit (603 €/month) other contribution rules apply; these numbers do not model them.
warnings.midijob: In the 2026 transition zone (603.01-2,000 €/month) employee contributions are reduced; these numbers apply the full rates.

notes: Wage tax, solidarity surcharge and church-tax base: the BMF's Programmablaufplan 2026 (bmf-steuerrechner.de, Stand 2025-10-23), run as is.

Social insurance 2026 (SV-Rechengrößenverordnung 2026): health 14.6% + the insurer's extra rate, pension 18.6%, unemployment 2.6%, care 3.6% (+0.6% childless, -0.25% per child from the second), insolvency levy 0.15%; ceilings 5,812.50 €/month (health, care) and 8,450 €/month (pension, unemployment).
U1/U2 depend on the insurer and are 0 until entered; accident insurance (BG) is not included.

calculators._doc_tone: #797 an output's `tone` is how the mockup's result box draws it: total (bold), minus (a deduction, red), result (the answer, green bold), detail (an indented line of the one above, small); none = a plain row.

social_2026._doc: SV-Rechengrößenverordnung 2026 (BGBl. 26 Nov 2025) as summarised by lohn-info.de/sozialversicherungsbeitraege2026.html, read 2026-10-02. PayslipTest holds bbg_* and the pension/unemployment halves equal to the values the BMF's PAP 2026 itself carries (MPARA), so the two declarations cannot drift. Rates in percent (totals; the payslip splits them), limits in euro.

ai._doc: The AI chat (Search ▸ AI chat). OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible chat completions; the token is the fleet Account's, read with libs:text-tools TextToolsClient.revealAiKey(account_provider) for each send and never stored or logged by this app. The model list is the live catalogue (models_url, cached catalog_ttl_hours); a model whose supported_parameters list native_web_param searches the web natively, any other model searches through the `web_plugin` plugin when the Web toggle is on. Verified against the live catalogue on 2026-10-02 (465 models; 19 with web_search_options, openrouter/auto among them).
ai.title: cloud-search

search._doc_subpages: #797 a subpage is a tab of the sub-nav under a vertical's title; a vertical with one subpage draws no sub-nav (the mockup's Search, Groceries and Things). `assistant` is the mockup's one Search page: the four engine boxes and the AI chat together. Saved Items is not a subpage: it is the menu's own view of everything starred.
search._doc_engines: #797 each engine box of the Search page: `icon` is a Phosphor name (ui/IconCatalog), `accent` a colour name in res/values/colors.xml (the mockup's per-engine tint). Every engine opens its own results page in cloud-browser; none is scraped.

things._doc: #903 The Things page (subpage kind `things`): the stores around the person that sell an item's kind, and what each asks for it. AREA: a coarse location fix (permission asked once) or the city typed in settings, default radius_km, adjustable in settings. STORES: OpenStreetMap shop=* through the Overpass API (keyless, ODbL; the public instances in overpass_urls are tried in order, because any one of them is sometimes overloaded) within the radius, cached per area/category for stores_ttl_hours; the item is matched to shop types by `categories[].words` (a word may sit inside a compound, 'bohr' in 'Bohrmaschine'); an item no category names falls back to `fallback`, and the page says so. PRICES, only what a source published: (1) Open Prices shelf prices seen at that very OSM place (receipt or price tag, dated; groceries and drugstore goods mostly), (2) the online price a chain's own site publishes, read server-side by scrappers-api GET /prices (robots.txt-gated, JSON-LD offers; needs the fleet bearer; see user-data_scrappers-api/src/code/prices.json for the chains and why the others are off). A store with neither shows no price and why; nothing is estimated.

agents._doc: #913 the Agents page (draft-only agents). Cloud Search READS through two read-only fleet doors (engines) and never submits, posts or sends anything: an agent produces a DRAFT and the person copies it and sends it themselves. Every agent must say mode draft_only or the declaration is refused. This block is also the contract with the engines (each engine's own constants are held equal to it by ac_cloud-mail/test/test-mail-agent-door.sh and ac_cloud-browser/test/test-browser-agent-door.sh and by the JVM suite).

mail._doc: Cloud Mail's query-only provider (ac_cloud-mail app.sterna.agentapi). Authority is <mail package>.<authority_suffix>; the package is the fleet row `fleet`.

browser._doc: Cloud Browser's open activity and read-only fetch provider (ac_cloud-browser cloudbrowser.agentapi). Authority is <browser package>.<authority_suffix>.

defaults._doc: A run's starting values; Settings overrides model and the budgets. Budgets are US dollars: a model call that could pass the per-run or the per-day cap is not made. unknown_price_per_token prices a model the catalogue does not list a plain price for (a router), deliberately high.

profile_fields.label: About you
profile_fields.hint: 2-3 lines; the only facts the model may use about you

agents.label: House search
agents.blurb: Reads your wg-gesucht.de alert mails, opens each new listing, and drafts an application from your template. You copy it and send it yourself.

links._doc: A link counts only when its host is one of hosts (or a subdomain) and its path ends in the listing's id (id_regex group 1); the query string is dropped; a listing is one id however many links name it. exclude_paths are account and messaging pages, never a listing.

templates.label: Room application (German)

cloud._doc: #913 the Cloud Search section (Apps, Messages, Code): the parts of the fleet this app can search honestly. Apps searches the constellation manifest (baked from aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json, kind app) and opens the app; Messages searches Cloud Mail through the read-only agent door; Code has no search engine in the fleet yet, so it opens Cloud Code and searches the owner's repositories on GitHub in Cloud Browser.

ui._doc: The shell: build.json::search drives every list; ui holds only the chrome's own settings.
ui._doc_debug_api: Routes on the fleet debug API (libs:devtools AppDebugServer), for checks with the screen locked: /api/search/verticals (every vertical, subpage, source with its kind/enabled/why), /api/search/query?v=&q=&city= (the real query through the same engine and cache the screens use: listings + per-source status), /api/search/calc?name=&<field>=... (a calculator's outputs and warnings), /api/search/analysis?v= (#797: the jobs statistics or the market series, with each source's status), /api/search/feed?v= (the Feed page's headlines and each feed's status). The ops never include `state` (update-ack-guard owns GET /api/state). #913: /api/search/agents (the agents, their last run, the budget), /api/search/runs (the run log with its audit lines), /api/search/reports and /api/search/report?id= (what agents published), /api/search/cloud?kind=apps|messages&q= (the Cloud Search section).
ui._doc_nav: #868 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island (Web Search, Cloud Search, Chat, Agents, Reports; the first two read Web and Cloud on the island because two two-word labels do not fit five cells at 360 dp - the lib's label fitting never settles - and the top pill names them in full from res/values/strings.xml), ui.sections[] what each item opens, ui.default_section where the app opens. A section's pages are its PageTabs strip: Web Search's pages are the search.verticals it covers (House, Jobs, Groceries, Things; each with its own subpage strip one level lower), Cloud Search's are Apps, Messages and Code, Chat is today's Search page (the assistant vertical), Agents has Agents, Runs, Templates and Settings, Reports lists what agents published. test-search-shell.sh S10 holds the declaration, search.verticals and search.subpages together.
